text: First form of Navadurga: Sri Shailaputri Devi
Why does the Navaratri worship begin with the daughter of the king of mountains?
Among the Navadurgas, the first form is Sri Shailaputri Devi.
Shailamu means mountain.
Putri means daughter.
Goddess Parvati, who was born as the daughter of Himavan, the king of mountains, is worshipped as Shailaputri Devi.
According to mythological narratives, the Goddess, who was born as Sati Devi, the daughter of Daksha Prajapati in her previous birth, later incarnated as the daughter of Himavan.
What is the specialty of the Goddess's form?
Shailaputri Devi appears on a bull vehicle.
She holds a trident in one hand and a lotus in the other.
While the trident reminds us of her power, the lotus symbolizes purity.
So, what is the significance of worshipping this form on the first day?
Shailaputri worship is associated with the idea that just as a mountain stands firmly, our devotion should also be equally stable.
The first step for the nine-day spiritual practice of Navaratri,
stable faith.
firm resolve.
unwavering devotion towards the Goddess.
Om Devi Shailaputryai Namah ॥
Let us pray to the Goddess to bestow courage that stands like a mountain,
and unwavering devotion.
